mainEntity.name: What lighting options are best for a home library?

acceptedAnswer.text: Effective lighting in a home library combines ambient, task, and accent lighting to create a comfortable and functional space. Recessed lighting or track lighting can provide general illumination. Task lighting, such as under-shelf LED strips or strategically placed reading lamps, is crucial for reducing eye strain. Accent lighting can highlight specific architectural features or book collections. A key decision factor is the primary use of the library; a space primarily for reading requires more focused task lighting, while a display-oriented library might prioritize accent lighting to showcase collections. Dimmer switches are also a versatile addition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Optimal home library lighting combines ambient, task (e.g., under-shelf LEDs), and accent lighting. The best choice depends on whether the library is for reading or display, and dimmer switches are versatile.
